I think another good point to bring up is the fact that FPS has become a go to game mechanic for the majority of game developers. Wow, isn't it neat how they're all 3 letter accronyms?

I think another good point to bring up is the fact that FPS has become a go to game mechanic for the majority of game developers.

My take on this is due to the whole "games must be gritty!" movement. In order to make a game seem adult and not for "casual kiddies" etc. The FPS genre is often seen as an easy way to have grittiness without actually adding any kind of dark, morally-involved or otherwise "adult" content. I wish more games were created like Psychonauts, which goes into some pretty dark themes beyond the humour - despite how it is a 3D action platformer where there isn't even that much "action". I think developers (well, AAA developers) could adapt existing stories and themes to different genres, adding more depth due to the differing mechanics.

The problem is though that a lot of gamers might be used to the FPS/Brawler/First Person RPG trend so much that they won't be able to get used to a genre they are unfamiliar with even if it is the same franchise. It's kind of like an infinite loop - big developers only push out games in certain genres, gamers get used to this, developers have to do this etc.

That is true. And not a lot of things have made me laugh more than the fact that you can present a kid with a character who goes on a murderous revenge filled rampage and parents will turn a blind eye but god forbid you include a naked human in the game and "OMG Jimmy don't look!".

But back to the point: I don't think the players won't be able to get used to any other genre as much as the fact that the vast majority of developers simply won't DARE to go deviate from the formula. Why should they, when any networked mouse look script with nice graphics is bound to make a profit? There are tons of games that don't follow this formula like Portal and Minecraft which are loved by masses comparable to FPS enthusiasts.

I'm sure recent games like Call of Duty and Evolve have interesting mechanics too, but, at least in my eyes, these just mask the fact that they're playing the same Tetris, but with different shaped blocks. Then again, this is all opinion based and I'm sure someone could come along and say the same about my Age of Empires II :)
